seo.title: Website migrations that protect SEO and working URLs
seo.description: Plan redirects, protect important pages, and test the new website before launch.

hero.title: Move your website without losing what already works.
hero.summary: We protect important URLs, search traffic, and customer journeys while the new site is built.
fit: Moving a marketing site to Next.js
Rebranding or changing the site structure
Replacing a CMS without losing useful content
hero.primaryGoal: Ship the new site without breaking the paths people and search engines already trust.

risks.title: Most migration mistakes happen behind the scenes.
risks.introduction: A polished redesign can still lose traffic or break customer journeys. These are the three failures we guard against.

items.title: Old links stop working
items.description: Useful pages vanish or redirect to the homepage. Visitors hit dead ends, and search engines lose the old page's context.

items.title: Important pages become generic
items.description: Different pages get the same titles and vague opening copy. Their purpose becomes harder to understand.

items.title: Test settings go live
items.description: A noindex rule, temporary domain, test analytics key, or old brand name slips into production.

solution.title: Five things we do before the switch.
solution.introduction: Each step leaves something concrete to review. No mystery. No last-minute SEO cleanup.

items.title: Build one list of the old site.
items.description: We combine the sitemap, crawl, analytics, Search Console, CMS, and backlink data. This catches valuable pages that normal navigation misses.
highlights: Mark pages with traffic, links, or leads
Include files, forms, and campaign URLs

items.title: Give every old URL a clear future.
items.description: Each old path gets one outcome: keep, move, combine, or remove. Redirects go straight to the closest useful page.
highlights: Record the reason for each choice

items.title: Improve the page without losing its purpose.
items.description: We keep the topic people came for, then improve the page. Titles, H1s, opening copy, and internal links are checked first.
highlights: Review the title, description, H1, and opening
Carry over useful links and media

items.title: Check the real site before it goes live.
items.description: We crawl the final environment and compare it with the approved URL map. We also test forms, analytics, canonicals, robots, and the sitemap.
highlights: Run the crawl against the final site
Check redirects, canonicals, robots, and sitemap

items.title: Catch problems early after launch.
items.description: We check old and new URLs as soon as the site moves. Then we watch crawl errors, landing-page traffic, and conversions for the first few weeks.
highlights: Check key routes in the first 24 hours
Compare traffic and conversions by landing page
Keep useful redirects for at least a year

method.title: A simple order of work.
method.introduction: The design can be ambitious. The migration process should be easy to follow.

steps.title: List the old site
steps.description: Gather URLs, traffic, links, forms, files, and campaign pages.

steps.title: Decide every URL
steps.description: Choose what stays, moves, combines, or goes away.

steps.title: Build one route at a time
steps.description: Keep each page's copy, metadata, links, and layout together.

steps.title: Test, launch, watch
steps.description: Crawl the final site, verify the map, then monitor the move.

items.title: A finished URL map
items.description: Every important old path has a clear destination or an intentional removal.

items.title: Pages that still make sense
items.description: Key pages keep their topic, links, metadata, and useful content.

items.title: A launch record
items.description: The team knows what passed, what needs an owner, and what to watch after launch.

faq.title: Common questions.
faq.introduction: Short answers to the decisions that usually slow a migration down.

items.question: Can you promise rankings will not change?
items.answer: No. Any major site change can affect search performance. We reduce avoidable risk, keep useful signals, and make problems easier to spot and fix.

items.question: Does every old URL need a redirect?
items.answer: No. Every important URL needs a decision. Redirect it only when there is a relevant replacement. Otherwise, use a clear 404 or 410.

items.question: When should we start the URL map?
items.answer: Before the new navigation and routes are final. Early mapping finds content gaps while the new structure is still easy to change.

items.question: How long should redirects stay?
items.answer: At least a year. Keep them longer when old URLs still receive traffic or links.

closing.title: Start with the URL map. Then build.
closing.description: Understand the old site before changing its routes. That one step makes the redesign faster and the launch safer.
